subject: Operational escalation — CloudNova tail-latency surge & customer update timeline
messages:
From: Joanna Lane <joanna.lane@cloudnova.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:12:34 -0700
Subject: Spike in tail-latency this morning — urgent

Irene —

We started seeing a spike in tail-latency on the /v1/generate endpoint around 07:50 PT. Error rate also climbed briefly (5-7% for ~12m). Our user-facing dashboard shows timeouts for some requests; this is impacting the content generation feature in production. We rolled forward a retry but the UX is degraded.

Attached is a CSV export of sample request traces and a screenshot of the error spike. Can you confirm whether this is on your side or if it's a configuration change we should revert? This is high priority for our SRE and product teams.

— Joanna
Senior Product Ops, CloudNova
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:22:11 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Spike in tail-latency this morning — urgent

Forwarding CloudNova alert — they observed a tail-latency and short error-rate spike on /v1/generate around 07:50 PT. They attached traces.

- Connor: please gather recent infra metrics (GPU queue depths, batch sizes, autoscaler actions) for 07:30–08:30 PT and paste here.
- Rishi: start a focused log dig on model-serving layer for the same timeframe (kv cache evictions, OOMs, kernel timeouts).
- Marissa/Laura: we need an executive-facing status and a proposed customer update timeline. Joanna is anxious; let's coordinate a brief customer message within 90 minutes.

I will open a private meeting bridge and post invite in channel.

Thanks —
Irene

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:31:49 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in tail-latency this morning — urgent

Quick notes from metrics (07:30–08:30 PT window):
- Peak p99 increased from baseline ~420ms to ~1.8s at 07:52.
- Error rate bump corresponds to 07:51–07:59 window (max ~6.3%).
- Autoscaler triggered two scale-ups for the dedicated pool at 07:48 and 07:53; both completed successfully.
- Observed a sharp increase in request concurrency on one host (host-21) and elevated GPU queue length on that host during the spike.
- No immediate signs of global KV cache eviction events, but local cache pressure on host-21 noted.

I dumped kernel-time logs and attached a short CSV with sampled latencies and host ids.

Connor
SRE — Serving Runtime
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:49:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in tail-latency this morning — urgent

Investigation summary:
- Host-21 experienced a transient GPU kernel scheduler stall at 07:51:02 that blocked a subset of batching workers for ~6s; this caused delayed token generation and retried client requests compounded the queue.
- Root cause appears to be an older GPU driver scheduled on host-21 (driver 510.x) that regressed with recent micro-ops on the 2.1 kernel path. Other hosts are on 515.x and show normal behavior.
- No model changes, no config rollouts from CloudNova or our infra during the incident window.

Action items executed:
1) Isolated host-21 from routing (drain) at 07:58.
2) Rolled a hotfix scheduling parameter to reduce single-host worker saturation — immediate p99 improved to ~550ms.
3) Plan: schedule controlled driver upgrade on host-21 and audit other hosts still on 510.x.

I recommend we tell the customer we isolated the host and applied a mitigation; next steps are driver upgrades and longer-term kernel-scheduler fix.

Rishi
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Lane <joanna.lane@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:12:03 -0700
Subject: Redwood status update: brief timeline & next steps

Joanna —

Thank you for flagging this. High level update:
- What happened: a single host (host-21) experienced a GPU kernel scheduler stall that briefly increased tail-latency and led to a short error-rate bump. No model or customer-side config changes were detected.
- What we did: we drained host-21 and applied an immediate scheduling mitigation at 07:58 PT which reduced p99 back near baseline (~550ms).
- Next steps (we will complete these and keep you informed):
  1) Controlled driver upgrade on host-21 and audit remaining hosts on older drivers — ETA 24 hours.
  2) Deploy a kernel-scheduler patch in canary tomorrow; timing TBD pending validation.
  3) Provide a post-incident report with logs, timeline, and remediation steps within 48 hours.

Proposed customer-facing timeline:
- 16:30 PT (in 90 minutes): brief note confirming containment and immediate mitigation (we can send this now if you want).
- 18:00 PT: update with root-cause summary and the mitigation we executed.
- Within 48 hours: full post-incident report and action items.

Please confirm if you'd like us to send the 16:30 PT note to your broader SRE/product mailing list (we can include the short CSV and screenshot). We will keep this bridge open and will post the incident doc link here.

Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
